hook: A $16 plug-in sconce is trending. Does it work?

scenes.visual_prompt: Thumb scrolling an Amazon best-sellers list, cursor landing on a plug-in antique sconce listing
scenes.on_screen_text: This $16 light has been Top 20 all September
scenes.voiceover: This plug-in sconce has been sitting in Amazon's top 20 lighting picks for most of September.

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of a bronze plug-in sconce glowing warm in a wall outlet, hallway background
scenes.voiceover: It's $14 to $18, plugs straight into the wall, and needs zero tools to install.

scenes.visual_prompt: Wide shot of a dark hallway with only the sconce lit on one wall, floor still dark
scenes.on_screen_text: But it lights a WALL, not your path
scenes.voiceover: Here's what the reviews keep flagging: it lights the wall next to it, not the floor you're actually walking on.

scenes.visual_prompt: Motion-sensor night light clicking on automatically as a foot steps near it in a hallway
scenes.voiceover: An $11.99 motion-sensor plug-in covers the part the sconce can't.

scenes.visual_prompt: Overhead shot of both lights working together in the same hallway at night
scenes.voiceover: The fix isn't picking one light — it's stacking two cheap ones.

scenes.visual_prompt: Text card on screen listing both products with prices adding to a total
scenes.voiceover: Two lights, twenty-eight dollars, and the hallway actually works after dark.

caption: I didn't buy the viral $16 sconce — I read what the review data across this whole category actually says first. Here's what a dark hallway needs (spoiler: it's two lights, not one). Full breakdown on the blog, link in bio.
